Unmarshal function always returns nil error

#### Description

The `Unmarshal` function in the API always returns `nil` instead of propagating actual errors from the underlying unmarshal operation. This means that invalid JSON, type mismatches, and other unmarshal errors are silently ignored.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/bytedance/sonic"
)

func main() {
    var result map[string]interface{}
    
    // This should return an error for invalid JSON
    err := sonic.Unmarshal([]byte("invalid json"), &result)
    fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", err) // Expected: syntax error, Got: <nil>
    
    // This should return an error for type mismatch
    var num int
    err = sonic.Unmarshal([]byte(`"string"`), &num)
    fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", err) // Expected: type error, Got: <nil>
    
    // This should return an error for empty string
    err = sonic.Unmarshal([]byte(""), &result)
    fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", err) // Expected: syntax error, Got: <nil>
}
```

All of these cases should return appropriate errors but instead return `nil`, making it impossible to detect when unmarshaling fails.
